title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The generation that followed, continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming, with Claude 4 models showing substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision. Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5/4.6, and Opus 4.5/4.6/4.7 all remain active (non-deprecated) as of mid-2026, even as newer defaults have shipped above them.

---

## Claude 4.7–4.8 and the Sonnet 5 / Mythos-Class Era (2026)

Through the first half of 2026, Anthropic kept iterating within Claude 4 before introducing a new capability tier above Opus.

**Claude Opus 4.7 (mid-April 2026)** became the new default for Max and Team Premium plans. It introduced an `xhigh` effort level — recommended for most coding work — and an interactive `/effort` slider in Claude Code.

**Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)** followed about six weeks later, fixing comment-verbosity and tool-calling regressions seen in 4.7. Anthropic reports it is roughly **four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in its own code pass unremarked**, and it shipped **dynamic workflows** (research preview): Claude plans a task, writes an orchestration script, and runs dozens to hundreds of subagents within a single Claude Code session. Pricing held steady at $5/$25 per MTok standard, $10/$50 fast mode.

**Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 (June 9, 2026)** introduced a new **"Mythos-class"** tier — Anthropic's most capable models to date, state-of-the-art on nearly every benchmark Anthropic tracks, and able to work autonomously for **days at a time** in an agent harness (planning across stages, delegating to sub-agents, checking their own work). Fable 5 is the publicly released, safeguarded version, with queries on some topics automatically redirected to Opus 4.8 (triggering in under 5% of sessions). Mythos 5 — the same underlying weights with some safeguards lifted — is offered only to a small group of vetted cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers. Both are priced at $10/$50 per MTok, less than half the price of the earlier Mythos Preview. Rollout was briefly interrupted: US-government-directed suspension on June 12, 2026, followed by a global redeployment restart on July 1, 2026.

**Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)** became the new default model for Free, Pro, Team Standard, and Enterprise seats. It substantially closes the gap with Opus 4.8 on reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work while priced at Sonnet rates, with a **native 1M-token context window** (5x the prior 200K standard) and up to 128K output tokens, adaptive thinking on by default. Introductory pricing is $2/$10 per MTok through August 31, 2026, rising to $3/$15 afterward.

**Active model line-up (July 2026):**

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest active tier |
| Sonnet 4.5 / 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Active, superseded as default by Sonnet 5 |
| **Sonnet 5** | `claude-sonnet-5` | **Current default**, 1M context, $2/$10 per MTok intro |
| Opus 4.5 / 4.6 / 4.7 | — | Active, not deprecated |
| **Opus 4.8** | `claude-opus-4-8` | Top general-availability model below Mythos-class |
| **Fable 5** | `claude-fable-5` | Mythos-class, public; ~5% of sessions redirected to Opus 4.8 |
| Mythos 5 | — | Fable 5 weights, safeguards relaxed; restricted access |

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → **1M tokens** (Sonnet 5, June 2026)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → **Mythos-class tier added above Opus (2026)**
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing (Sonnet 5 approaches Opus 4.8 quality at Sonnet pricing)
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems — Mythos-class models can now run autonomously for multiple days inside an agent harness
